automatic.answer: This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript service for finding the insertion position of a target in a sorted array—the first index with a value greater than or equal to the target. Its architecture has two layers: src/core.mjs exports the synchronous solve(nums, target) binary search, and src/service.mjs exposes execute as a thin forwarding wrapper. It uses ES modules and Node’s built-in test runner, with one smoke test through the service layer; the current implementation returns zero for empty input but incorrectly returns the last index instead of nums.length when the target exceeds every value.

automatic.answer: This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript service that finds the insertion position for a target in a sorted array—the first index with a value greater than or equal to the target. Its architecture has two layers: `src/core.mjs` exports the synchronous binary-search function `solve(nums, target)`, and `src/service.mjs` exposes `execute` as a thin forwarding wrapper. Tests use Node’s built-in test runner through `npm test`; the single smoke test covers an exact match, but the current implementation incorrectly returns the last index instead of the array length when the target exceeds every value.

This is a dependency-free JavaScript service that finds the first index in a sorted array whose value is at least the target, returning the array length if none exists and zero for empty input.

Its architecture has two layers: `src/core.mjs` exports the synchronous binary-search function `solve(nums, target)`, and `src/service.mjs` exposes `execute` as a thin forwarding wrapper. The current implementation correctly searches with `hi = nums.length` in O(log n) time and O(1) extra space. Tests run through Node’s built-in runner with `npm test`, although the single smoke test covers only an exact match.
